title: AM2 / AM2E — Installation Electrician EPA
subtitle: Two AM2 mock tests
description: A comprehensive AM2 knowledge exam set with two full mocks covering safe isolation, statutory duties, installation practice, inspection and testing, fault diagnosis and commissioning judgement.

scoring.label: Strong — ready for AM2 knowledge-style questions
Pass — review the missed AM2 source questions
Near miss — revise safe isolation, testing and installation duties
Major gaps — rebuild practical-assessment fundamentals first

priorities: Safe isolation, proving dead, lock-off and statutory safety duties.
Installation standards, containment, conductor identification and protective devices.
Inspection, testing, commissioning and certification decisions.
Fault diagnosis and practical judgement under assessment-style wording.
Treat each answer as a site decision, not a memory shortcut.

questions.prompt: Which statutory regulations impose specific duties to prevent danger from electrical systems and equipment at work?

options.A: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002

questions.explanation: The Electricity Supply Regulations 1988 have been replaced by the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002. The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 remain the specific workplace regulations concerned with preventing electrical danger.

A.text: ESQCR principally regulates the safety, quality and continuity of public electricity supplies; it is not the workplace electrical-duty regime described here.

B.text: The Electricity Supply Regulations 1988 have been replaced by the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002. The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 remain the specific workplace regulations concerned with preventing electrical danger.

C.text: The Factories Act is broad workplace legislation and is not the current set of specific electrical-system duties applied across workplaces.

D.text: BS 7671 is an influential non-statutory installation standard. It does not itself impose the statutory workplace duties in this prompt.

questions.prompt: An HSE inspector finds defective emergency lights that breach legal requirements, but the defect does not create a risk of serious personal injury requiring the activity to stop. The contravention is likely to continue unless it is remedied. Which notice is appropriate?
questions.explanation: The original facts do not determine the notice: prohibition depends on a risk of serious personal injury, whereas an improvement notice depends on a contravention likely to continue or recur. The revised facts match the statutory test for an improvement notice.

A.text: Immediate site closure is not the statutory response supported by these facts, which expressly exclude the serious-injury risk needed to stop an activity.

B.text: Deferring a prohibition changes when it takes effect, not its serious-personal-injury test. That test is expressly absent here.

C.text: A prohibition notice addresses an activity involving a risk of serious personal injury. The stated continuing contravention instead meets the improvement-notice test.

D.text: The original facts do not determine the notice: prohibition depends on a risk of serious personal injury, whereas an improvement notice depends on a contravention likely to continue or recur. The revised facts match the statutory test for an improvement notice.

questions.prompt: Which diagram uses standard symbols to show a circuit's components and electrical connections without representing their physical positions?
questions.explanation: Circuit diagram and schematic diagram are commonly used as synonyms, while a wiring diagram may also show connections, so the original options were not mutually exclusive. The revised alternatives distinguish a symbolic circuit diagram from physical-layout drawings.

A.text: A block diagram represents functions or subsystems as blocks and their broad relationships, rather than showing each circuit component and connection.

B.text: Circuit diagram and schematic diagram are commonly used as synonyms, while a wiring diagram may also show connections, so the original options were not mutually exclusive. The revised alternatives distinguish a symbolic circuit diagram from physical-layout drawings.

C.text: A layout diagram communicates the physical arrangement or placement of equipment, which the prompt specifically says is not being represented.

D.text: A site plan locates buildings, routes or equipment across a site; it is not the symbolic component-and-connection representation of a circuit.

questions.prompt: A location drawing is scaled at 1:50. A cable route measures 85 mm on the drawing. What is its actual length?
questions.explanation: The original prompt omitted punctuation between the measured and actual lengths. At 1:50, 85 mm represents 4250 mm, or 4.25 m.

A.text: Seventeen metres would represent 340 mm at 1:50. Multiplying the measured 85 mm by 50 gives only 4250 mm.

B.text: The original prompt omitted punctuation between the measured and actual lengths. At 1:50, 85 mm represents 4250 mm, or 4.25 m.

C.text: This value introduces an extra factor of ten: 85 mm multiplied by 50 is 4250 mm, which converts to 4.25 m rather than 42.5 m.

D.text: This appears to use an unrelated operation on the scale. A 1:50 drawing requires multiplication by 50, producing 4250 mm or 4.25 m.

questions.prompt: The preferred method of instructing the client in the correct use and maintenance of electrical equipment used within an installation would be to:

options.A: Leave relevant manufacturer's literature adjacent to equipment
options.B: Provide them with a guided tour and verbal instructions during the handover period
options.C: Provide them with an operations and maintenance manual
options.D: Provide them with the manufacturer's catalogue

questions.explanation: An operations and maintenance manual gives the client lasting written instructions for safe use, servicing and maintenance. Verbal handover alone is too easy to forget or misinterpret.

A.text: Loose literature beside equipment is incomplete, easily lost and does not consolidate installation-specific instructions.

B.text: A verbal tour is useful support but leaves no durable reference for later operators or maintainers.

C.text: An operations and maintenance manual gives the client lasting written instructions for safe use, servicing and maintenance. Verbal handover alone is too easy to forget or misinterpret.

D.text: A catalogue is a sales document covering many products, not an installation-specific operating and maintenance record.

questions.prompt: Which set of values satisfies the overload-coordination condition Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz?
questions.explanation: The full overload requirements also include the protective device's conventional operating-current condition I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz. The options only test Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz, so the prompt now states the condition actually assessed.

A.text: The full overload requirements also include the protective device's conventional operating-current condition I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz. The options only test Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz, so the prompt now states the condition actually assessed.

B.text: Here In is 20 A while Iz is only 18 A, so the protective-device rating exceeds the cable's current-carrying capacity.

C.text: Although the design current is below the device rating, the 10 A rating exceeds the cable capacity of 8 A and breaks In ≤ Iz.

D.text: The 20 A design current is greater than the 15 A protective-device rating, so this set fails the first relationship Ib ≤ In.

questions.prompt: A heater taking 40A is supplied by a cable 10m long. If the cable has a volt drop of 4mV per ampere per metre, the voltage drop in the cable will be:
questions.explanation: Volt drop is mV per amp per metre multiplied by current and length. 4 x 40 x 10 = 1600 mV, which is 1.6 V.

A.text: 0.16 V omits a factor of ten: 4 mV/A/m × 40 A × 10 m equals 1600 mV.

B.text: Volt drop is mV per amp per metre multiplied by current and length. 4 x 40 x 10 = 1600 mV, which is 1.6 V.

C.text: 16 V treats the millivolt result as though another factor of ten remained after converting to volts.

D.text: 8 V does not follow the cable-drop product and is five times the calculated 1.6 V.

questions.prompt: Which domestic accessory would you expect to have terminals labelled, N, Loop and S/L:
questions.explanation: A ceiling rose commonly has neutral, permanent loop and switched-line terminals. The S/L terminal feeds the lamp after the wall switch.

A.text: A ceiling rose commonly has neutral, permanent loop and switched-line terminals. The S/L terminal feeds the lamp after the wall switch.

B.text: A consumer unit uses neutral bars and circuit protective-device terminals rather than a luminaire switched-line terminal marked S/L.

C.text: A generic junction box has numbered or purpose-assigned terminals but not the standard loop-in ceiling-rose grouping.

D.text: A socket is marked line, neutral and earth; it has no switched-line lighting terminal.

questions.prompt: A motor is connected to a starter through flexible metallic conduit that has not been selected or verified for use as a protective conductor. How should protective-conductor continuity be provided?

options.B: The flexible conduit provided the conduit boxes are scraped and locknuts are used
options.C: The flexible conduit without any further modification

questions.explanation: BS 7671 can permit a metallic conduit system to serve as a protective conductor when it is suitable and verified, so flexible conduit alone is not universally disallowed. With suitability expressly unverified, a separate circuit protective conductor is the dependable answer.

A.text: BS 7671 can permit a metallic conduit system to serve as a protective conductor when it is suitable and verified, so flexible conduit alone is not universally disallowed. With suitability expressly unverified, a separate circuit protective conductor is the dependable answer.

B.text: Good terminations alone do not establish that this flexible conduit has suitable impedance, mechanical reliability and verified continuity as a protective conductor.

C.text: The prompt states that the conduit has not been selected or verified for the protective-conductor function, so relying on it alone leaves continuity unproven.

D.text: A neutral is a current-carrying live conductor in normal service and must not be substituted for the circuit protective conductor in this installation.

questions.prompt: Cables not likely to be affected by electrical interference are:
questions.explanation: Fibre-optic cable transmits light rather than electrical signals. Because it is non-metallic, electromagnetic interference does not normally affect it.

A.text: Coaxial shielding reduces interference, but the metallic conductor can still couple electromagnetic energy and ground-potential effects.

B.text: Fibre-optic cable transmits light rather than electrical signals. Because it is non-metallic, electromagnetic interference does not normally affect it.

C.text: Shielded twisted pairs reject interference well, but they remain conductive copper transmission paths.

D.text: Screened cable provides additional rejection yet can still experience electromagnetic coupling and screen-current issues.

questions.prompt: Under BS 5839-1, what is the normal minimum fire-alarm sound level throughout accessible areas where no higher level is required by background noise or sleeping risk?
questions.explanation: The required sound level depends on location and risk: the normal general minimum is 65 dB(A), but sleeping accommodation and high background noise can require more, and limited areas can use a specific relaxation. The qualification makes 65 dB(A) uniquely valid.

A.text: The required sound level depends on location and risk: the normal general minimum is 65 dB(A), but sleeping accommodation and high background noise can require more, and limited areas can use a specific relaxation. The qualification makes 65 dB(A) uniquely valid.

B.text: Seventy decibels may be designed for particular acoustic conditions, but it is not the normal general minimum stated for accessible areas.

C.text: Seventy-five decibels is associated with the higher level commonly needed at a bedhead to wake sleeping occupants, not the qualified general baseline.

D.text: Eighty decibels exceeds the normal minimum and may be unnecessarily intrusive; higher levels are selected from background noise and occupant risk.

questions.prompt: A heater provides 172.5 W of useful heat while drawing 2 A from a 230 V supply. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: The original wording does not say whether 172.5 W is input or useful output and leaves the supply voltage implicit. With 460 W input and 172.5 W useful output, the stated efficiency is 37.5%.

A.text: The electrical input is 230 V × 2 A = 460 W. Dividing 172.5 W by 460 W gives 0.375, not 0.266.

B.text: The original wording does not say whether 172.5 W is input or useful output and leaves the supply voltage implicit. With 460 W input and 172.5 W useful output, the stated efficiency is 37.5%.

C.text: This percentage is not the useful-output-to-input ratio. The stated powers give 172.5 ÷ 460 × 100 = 37.5%.

D.text: Seventy-five percent would require 345 W of useful output from a 460 W input, exactly twice the useful heat stated in the prompt.

questions.prompt: The effect of improving the power factor of a fluorescent lamp circuit is that the current taken from the supply is:

options.B: Lagging the supply voltage by a larger angle

questions.explanation: Improving power factor reduces the reactive current needed for the same useful power. The supply current therefore becomes smaller.

A.text: For the same real power and voltage, raising power factor reduces rather than increases apparent current.

B.text: Improvement reduces the phase angle between current and voltage instead of making current lag further.

C.text: Improving power factor reduces the reactive current needed for the same useful power. The supply current therefore becomes smaller.

D.text: Current would remain unchanged only if apparent power stayed fixed; compensation supplies some reactive current locally.

questions.prompt: For fire protection in agricultural or horticultural premises, the rated residual operating current of the RCD protecting a relevant circuit must not exceed:
questions.explanation: Current BS 7671 wording specifies RCD protection with a rated residual operating current not exceeding 300 mA for the relevant fire-protection requirement; it is not merely an optional use of an unspecified 'operating current'.

A.text: A 150 mA device is below the permitted ceiling and may be selected, but 150 mA is not the maximum rating set by this fire-protection rule.

B.text: Thirty milliamperes is widely used for additional personal protection. It is more sensitive than required here and is not the stated fire-protection ceiling.

C.text: Current BS 7671 wording specifies RCD protection with a rated residual operating current not exceeding 300 mA for the relevant fire-protection requirement; it is not merely an optional use of an unspecified 'operating current'.

D.text: A 500 mA rating is above the 300 mA maximum, so it may allow an earth-leakage heating fault to persist at too high a level.

questions.prompt: Under BS 7671, a non-flame-propagating conduit, cable-ducting or cable-trunking system providing at least IP33 may omit internal sealing at a fire-resisting penetration only when its internal cross-sectional area does not exceed:
questions.explanation: 'Cable delivery system' is a typo and the area alone is not the whole exception. Regulation 527.2.3 applies the 710 mm² limit together with non-flame-propagating construction and the required degree of protection.

A.text: A 700 mm² system is within the allowance, but it is not the specified upper boundary. The stated limit extends a further 10 mm².

B.text: 'Cable delivery system' is a typo and the area alone is not the whole exception. Regulation 527.2.3 applies the 710 mm² limit together with non-flame-propagating construction and the required degree of protection.

C.text: This is 10 mm² above the stated exception limit, so the qualifying system cannot rely on the no-internal-sealing allowance at this area.

D.text: This exceeds the 710 mm² boundary by 40 mm². The non-flame-propagating and IP33 conditions do not enlarge that area limit.

questions.prompt: Copper links are used across joints in metallic trunking installations in order to:

options.A: Increase the strength of the joint
options.B: Maintain the electrical continuity of the exposed conductive parts
options.C: Provide a temporary fixing before the main bolts are fitted

questions.explanation: Metallic trunking joints must remain electrically continuous so exposed metal can be earthed reliably. Copper links bridge the joint and maintain that continuity.

A.text: Mechanical fasteners and trunking construction provide joint strength; a flexible copper link is not a structural brace.

B.text: Metallic trunking joints must remain electrically continuous so exposed metal can be earthed reliably. Copper links bridge the joint and maintain that continuity.

C.text: A bonding link is fitted as a permanent low-impedance connection, not as an assembly aid removed after bolting.

D.text: Copper does not generally prevent dissimilar-metal corrosion; its purpose here is electrical rather than chemical protection.

questions.prompt: The purpose of segregated trunking is to:

options.A: Allow accommodation of circuits having different voltage bands
options.B: Prevent overheating in vertical trunking runs
options.C: Prevent the spread of fire within the trunking
options.D: Support the cables installed in the trunking

questions.explanation: Segregated trunking separates circuits of different voltage bands. This prevents unsuitable mixing of, for example, ELV/control wiring with low-voltage power circuits.

A.text: Segregated trunking separates circuits of different voltage bands. This prevents unsuitable mixing of, for example, ELV/control wiring with low-voltage power circuits.

B.text: Vertical-run overheating is controlled by current rating, grouping, ventilation and supports, not by service compartments alone.

C.text: Fire stopping is provided where containment penetrates barriers; ordinary segregation is not a longitudinal fire barrier.

D.text: The enclosure and cable supports carry the wiring; the divider's defining function is separation of incompatible circuits or services.

questions.prompt: PME (Protective Multiple Earthing) is mainly associated with which system of earthing:
questions.explanation: 'TI system' is a transposition typo. The recognized earthing-system designation is IT; PME remains associated with TN-C-S.

A.text: An IT system has its live conductors isolated from earth or earthed through impedance and does not use a distributor PEN conductor.

B.text: 'TI system' is a transposition typo. The recognized earthing-system designation is IT; PME remains associated with TN-C-S.

C.text: TN-S keeps neutral and protective conductors separate throughout and therefore is not the combined PEN arrangement of PME.

D.text: A TT installation relies on the consumer's earth electrode rather than a distributor-provided multiple-earthed PEN conductor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not itself a provision for basic protection?
questions.explanation: 'Direct contact' is superseded terminology. Insulation, barriers or enclosures, and placing out of reach provide basic protection; disconnection after a fault is part of fault protection under automatic disconnection of supply.

A.text: 'Direct contact' is superseded terminology. Insulation, barriers or enclosures, and placing out of reach provide basic protection; disconnection after a fault is part of fault protection under automatic disconnection of supply.

B.text: Barriers and enclosures prevent people touching live parts during normal service, so they are a recognized provision for basic protection.

C.text: Basic insulation forms the normal-service barrier between a person and a live conductor, making it a direct basic-protection measure.

D.text: Placing live parts outside the defined arm's-reach zone is a basic-protection provision used under the restricted conditions allowed by BS 7671.

questions.prompt: Where supplementary protective bonding between an exposed-conductive-part and an extraneous-conductive-part is required, what is the minimum copper conductor size when it has no mechanical protection, before any larger sizing requirement is considered?
questions.explanation: A sink or its water pipes do not automatically require supplementary bonding. Where supplementary bonding is actually required, an unprotected copper conductor has a 4 mm² minimum, subject to any larger size required by the connected protective conductors.

A.text: An unprotected 1.5 mm² copper bonding conductor is below the mechanical-robustness minimum; that size cannot satisfy the stated installation condition.

B.text: A 2.5 mm² copper supplementary bond can meet the baseline only when it has mechanical protection, which the prompt explicitly removes.

C.text: A sink or its water pipes do not automatically require supplementary bonding. Where supplementary bonding is actually required, an unprotected copper conductor has a 4 mm² minimum, subject to any larger size required by the connected protective conductors.

D.text: Six square millimetres may be required by a larger connected protective conductor or chosen for robustness, but it is not the unprotected baseline minimum.

questions.prompt: Which BS 7671 term describes protection against electric shock under single-fault conditions, including contact with an exposed-conductive-part made live by a fault?
questions.explanation: 'Indirect contact' is legacy terminology. Current BS 7671 calls protection under fault conditions 'fault protection', while basic protection addresses contact with live parts in normal service.

A.text: Additional protection supplements basic and fault protection when those measures may fail or users face increased risk; it is not the name for the single-fault layer itself.

B.text: Basic protection prevents contact with live parts in normal, fault-free service. The scenario instead starts after a fault energises exposed metal.

C.text: Functional earthing is provided for correct equipment or system operation, rather than as the defined shock-protection measure under a fault condition.

D.text: 'Indirect contact' is legacy terminology. Current BS 7671 calls protection under fault conditions 'fault protection', while basic protection addresses contact with live parts in normal service.

questions.prompt: Where a firefighter's switch is to be installed, in order to comply with BS 7671 it must be:

options.A: No more than 2.75 m from the ground with the off position at the bottom
options.B: No more than 2.75 m from the ground with the off position at the top
options.C: No more than 3.75 m from the ground with the off position at the bottom
options.D: No more than 3.75 m from the ground with the off position at the top

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch must be accessible and arranged so its state is clear in an emergency. BS 7671 sets the height limit at 2.75 m with the off position at the top.

A.text: The height is acceptable, but the operating handle must indicate OFF in the upper position rather than at the bottom.

B.text: A firefighter's switch must be accessible and arranged so its state is clear in an emergency. BS 7671 sets the height limit at 2.75 m with the off position at the top.

C.text: 3.75 m is above the maximum accessible mounting height and this option also reverses the required handle position.

D.text: The top OFF position is correct, but the proposed height exceeds 2.75 m.

questions.prompt: Circuit protective conductors are connected between:

options.B: The main earth terminal and exposed conductive parts
options.C: The main earth terminal and extraneous conductive parts
options.D: The main earth terminal and the earth rod

questions.explanation: A circuit protective conductor connects exposed conductive parts back to the main earthing terminal. That path allows fault current to operate the protective device.

A.text: Connections to extraneous-conductive-parts are protective bonding conductors, not the defining circuit protective conductor path.

B.text: A circuit protective conductor connects exposed conductive parts back to the main earthing terminal. That path allows fault current to operate the protective device.

C.text: The main earthing terminal to an extraneous service is a main protective bonding connection.

D.text: The main earthing terminal to an electrode is an earthing conductor, not a circuit protective conductor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following protective devices is used in domestic plug tops:
questions.explanation: Standard UK plug-top cartridge fuses are manufactured to BS 1362. BS 3036, BS 88 and BS EN 60898 apply to other protective devices.

A.text: Standard UK plug-top cartridge fuses are manufactured to BS 1362. BS 3036, BS 88 and BS EN 60898 apply to other protective devices.

B.text: BS 3036 covers semi-enclosed rewirable fuses used in older distribution equipment, not cartridge links for plugs.

C.text: BS 88 fuse systems protect distribution and industrial circuits and are physically different from a domestic plug fuse.

D.text: BS EN 60898 applies to circuit-breakers for household and similar installations, not replaceable plug-top fuse links.

questions.prompt: Fusing factor is the ratio of:
questions.explanation: Fusing factor compares the current that will actually fuse the element with the fuse's rated current. It is therefore fusing current divided by current rating.

A.text: This is the reciprocal of fusing factor and would normally produce a value below one.

B.text: Fault current affects operating time but is not the denominator used to define the device's fusing factor.

C.text: Fusing factor compares the current that will actually fuse the element with the fuse's rated current. It is therefore fusing current divided by current rating.

D.text: A ratio to the particular circuit fault current would vary by installation and would not characterise the fuse itself.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the National Grid:

options.A: Transmission of electricity from power stations to factories
options.B: Transmission of electricity from power stations to industrial locations
options.C: Transmission of electricity from power stations to substations
options.D: Transmission of electricity from sub stations to domestic premises

questions.explanation: The National Grid transmits electricity at high voltage from generating stations to substations. Local distribution then supplies factories, businesses and homes from those substations.

A.text: Factories normally receive electricity through a distribution network or dedicated connection downstream of transmission substations, not directly from every power station.

B.text: Industrial customers are end users served after network transformation and distribution; the transmission system's general role is not defined by one customer class.

C.text: The National Grid transmits electricity at high voltage from generating stations to substations. Local distribution then supplies factories, businesses and homes from those substations.

D.text: Moving electricity from substations to individual homes is the distribution network's role, after the high-voltage transmission stage.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of power stations does not use a fossil fuel to generate electricity:
questions.explanation: Nuclear power uses heat from nuclear fission rather than burning coal, oil or gas. Coal, gas and oil stations all use fossil fuels.

A.text: Coal is a carbon-rich fossil fuel burned to provide boiler heat.

B.text: Natural gas is a fossil fuel burned in turbines or combined-cycle plant.

C.text: Nuclear power uses heat from nuclear fission rather than burning coal, oil or gas. Coal, gas and oil stations all use fossil fuels.

D.text: Oil is a petroleum-derived fossil fuel even when used only for peak or backup generation.

questions.prompt: For an isolated a.c. generator running at constant speed on open circuit, increasing field excitation will cause the:
questions.explanation: Excitation raises terminal voltage for an isolated open-circuit generator, but on a grid-connected synchronous machine it primarily changes reactive power and power factor because grid voltage is imposed externally. The operating condition removes that ambiguity.

A.text: Generated frequency follows rotational speed and pole count. The prompt fixes speed, so changing excitation does not raise frequency.

B.text: A field-current change alters magnetic flux, not the fixed mechanical speed that determines frequency, so frequency does not fall either.

C.text: An open-circuit generator supplies essentially no load current, so load power factor is not the controlled outcome; excitation changes its terminal voltage.

D.text: Excitation raises terminal voltage for an isolated open-circuit generator, but on a grid-connected synchronous machine it primarily changes reactive power and power factor because grid voltage is imposed externally. The operating condition removes that ambiguity.

questions.prompt: Which listed renewable electricity system depends on a usable combination of water flow and head?
questions.explanation: Micro-hydro output depends on both water flow and head; it does not invariably require a 'large amount' of water because a higher head can compensate for lower flow. The revised wording tests the actual resource requirement.

A.text: Grey-water equipment conserves and reuses water; it is not an electricity generator whose available power is calculated from flow and head.

B.text: A wind turbine depends on wind-speed distribution, swept area and siting. Water head is not an input to its energy resource.

C.text: Micro-hydro output depends on both water flow and head; it does not invariably require a 'large amount' of water because a higher head can compensate for lower flow. The revised wording tests the actual resource requirement.

D.text: Photovoltaic modules convert solar irradiance directly into electricity, so their resource assessment concerns sunlight rather than water head and flow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following systems require separate pipework, storage and a filtration system for operation:
questions.explanation: Grey water recycling collects, stores, filters and redistributes used water. That requires separate pipework, storage and filtration equipment.

A.text: Grey water recycling collects, stores, filters and redistributes used water. That requires separate pipework, storage and filtration equipment.

B.text: A micro-wind installation needs a turbine, electrical conversion and support structure; it does not collect used water through storage and filtration pipework.

C.text: Micro-hydro uses a watercourse, intake, turbine and electrical equipment. A grey-water storage-and-filtration network is not intrinsic to its operation.

D.text: PV generation requires modules and electrical balance-of-system equipment, not tanks, filters and a second set of water-distribution pipes.

questions.prompt: A statutory regulation is:

options.B: Made under statutory authority and legally enforceable
options.C: Approved only by an electricity network operator
options.D: Issued only as non-statutory guidance by a professional body

questions.explanation: A statutory regulation has legal force because it is made under powers granted by legislation. It is not merely 'agreed by law', a standard, a network operator or a professional body.

A.text: BS 7671 is a technical standard and cannot agree or enact legislation. Statutory force comes from authority granted by legislation.

B.text: A statutory regulation has legal force because it is made under powers granted by legislation. It is not merely 'agreed by law', a standard, a network operator or a professional body.

C.text: A network operator can set connection requirements, but its approval alone does not create a regulation with general legal force.

D.text: Professional guidance can explain good practice but, by definition, non-statutory guidance is not itself a legally enforceable regulation.

questions.prompt: If a legal duty is absolute, it:

options.B: Must be met regardless of cost or other considerations
options.C: Must be met within an agreed time
options.D: Requires a competent electrician to complete

questions.explanation: The original hyphenation is malformed. HSE guidance explains that an unqualified absolute requirement must be met regardless of cost or other consideration, subject to any specific statutory defence.

A.text: An absolute statutory requirement is compulsory; it is the strongest form of duty and is not qualified by reasonable practicability.

B.text: The original hyphenation is malformed. HSE guidance explains that an unqualified absolute requirement must be met regardless of cost or other consideration, subject to any specific statutory defence.

C.text: A compliance deadline may appear in a notice or plan, but it does not define whether the underlying legal duty is absolute.

D.text: Competence may be required for particular work, yet an absolute duty describes the obligation's unqualified nature, not one occupation that must perform it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following documents is not produced by the client:
questions.explanation: A tender is normally produced by a contractor or supplier in response to the client's documents. Orders, specifications and variation orders can come from the client side of the contract process.

A.text: The client issues an order to accept or commission the contractor's work.

B.text: The client's specification states the required scope, performance and quality against which bids are prepared.

C.text: A tender is normally produced by a contractor or supplier in response to the client's documents. Orders, specifications and variation orders can come from the client side of the contract process.

D.text: A variation order is issued on the client or contract-administrator side to change the contracted work.

questions.prompt: A room measures 4.25 metres long, what would it measure on a drawing scaled at 1:20:
questions.explanation: 4.25 m is 425 cm. On a 1:20 drawing the dimension is 425 / 20 = 21.25 cm.

A.text: 0.2125 is the scaled length in metres, not centimetres; relabelling it as centimetres makes it 100 times too small.

B.text: 4.25 m is 425 cm. On a 1:20 drawing the dimension is 425 / 20 = 21.25 cm.

C.text: 212.5 cm applies the metre-to-centimetre conversion but fails to divide by the 1:20 scale.

D.text: 412 mm neither equals 4.25 m divided by 20 nor represents the correct scaled length of 212.5 mm.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of an assembly diagram is:

options.A: Show how the components fit together
options.B: To provide different views of the components
options.C: To show the sequence of control
options.D: Use symbols to represent circuit components and show their connections

questions.explanation: An assembly diagram is concerned with the physical arrangement of parts. It shows how components fit together rather than the circuit sequence.

A.text: An assembly diagram is concerned with the physical arrangement of parts. It shows how components fit together rather than the circuit sequence.

B.text: Individual component views show shape and dimensions but do not explain the relationship of parts in the completed assembly.

C.text: The sequence of control is functional information normally shown on a sequence chart or control schematic.

D.text: A symbolic connection diagram explains the circuit, whereas an assembly diagram explains physical fit and construction.

questions.prompt: For a 6 A BS EN 60898 Type B circuit-breaker, what current is used to ensure operation in its instantaneous tripping region?
questions.explanation: The original distractor '6:00 AM' is a data-corruption error. Type B instantaneous operation is assured using 5 In, so a 6 A device uses 30 A.

A.text: One hundred amperes is about 16.7 times the 6 A rating, far above the 5 In value used to ensure a Type B breaker's instantaneous operation.

B.text: One hundred and twenty-five amperes exceeds 20 In for this device and is unrelated to the upper instantaneous threshold specified for Type B operation.

C.text: The original distractor '6:00 AM' is a data-corruption error. Type B instantaneous operation is assured using 5 In, so a 6 A device uses 30 A.

D.text: Six amperes is only the breaker's nominal current In. It may be carried continuously and is not an instantaneous-trip test current.

questions.prompt: In the adiabatic equation S = √(I²t) / k, what does the symbol I represent?

options.B: R.m.s. fault current flowing through the protective device
options.C: Current rating of the protective device

questions.explanation: The radical and exponent were malformed and the prompt had a double colon. In the adiabatic equation, I is the effective r.m.s. fault current for a fault of negligible impedance that flows through the protective device.

A.text: Design current Ib is used for normal load and cable selection. The adiabatic check instead evaluates heating during the much larger fault current.

B.text: The radical and exponent were malformed and the prompt had a double colon. In the adiabatic equation, I is the effective r.m.s. fault current for a fault of negligible impedance that flows through the protective device.

C.text: The device rating In is not substituted for I in this equation; actual prospective r.m.s. fault current determines the energy let through before disconnection.

D.text: Normal load current does not create the short-duration fault heating assessed by I²t, so it is not the current represented by I.

questions.prompt: Which listed condition requires a clearly visible voltage warning notice before access to live parts?

options.B: Electric motors having a rating exceeding 0.37 kW
options.C: Equipment or an enclosure containing a nominal voltage exceeding 230 V to earth where that voltage is not normally expected
options.D: Switchgear which cannot normally be observed by the operator

questions.explanation: The BS 7671 requirement concerns a nominal voltage exceeding 230 V to earth where its presence is not normally expected, with the notice visible before access to live parts. The original wording omitted those limiting conditions.

A.text: Class II equipment is identified by its double-insulation marking. Its classification alone does not trigger this unexpected-voltage warning requirement.

B.text: Motor rating can affect isolation and control provisions, but a 0.37 kW threshold does not establish an unexpected voltage above 230 V to earth.

C.text: The BS 7671 requirement concerns a nominal voltage exceeding 230 V to earth where its presence is not normally expected, with the notice visible before access to live parts. The original wording omitted those limiting conditions.

D.text: Remote or unobserved switchgear can require suitable control and indication, yet that fact alone does not meet the stated high-voltage warning condition.

questions.prompt: Non-metallic conduit must only be used within suitable ranges of:
questions.explanation: Non-metallic conduit can soften, become brittle or lose performance outside its temperature range. Ambient temperature is therefore a key suitability limit.

A.text: Non-metallic conduit can soften, become brittle or lose performance outside its temperature range. Ambient temperature is therefore a key suitability limit.

B.text: Humidity may affect the complete installation, but ordinary conduit suitability is not expressed as an electrical humidity range in this choice set.

C.text: Load current determines cable heating and size; conduit itself carries no normal circuit current.

D.text: Voltage rating applies chiefly to cable insulation and system separation, while conduit performance is limited by environmental temperature.

questions.prompt: Highest frequency data transmission rates can be achieved by the use of:
questions.explanation: Fibre-optic systems carry data as pulses of light and have very high bandwidth. They achieve higher data rates than copper-based coaxial or screened twisted-pair cables.

A.text: Coaxial cable has useful bandwidth, but conductor loss and electromagnetic constraints limit it below modern optical links.

B.text: Fibre-optic systems carry data as pulses of light and have very high bandwidth. They achieve higher data rates than copper-based coaxial or screened twisted-pair cables.

C.text: Shielded twisted-pair copper reduces interference yet has substantially lower bandwidth-distance capability than optical fibre.

D.text: Screened cable remains a metallic transmission medium and does not match optical carrier bandwidth or immunity.

questions.prompt: For emergency escape lighting in premises that may be reoccupied immediately after the normal supply is restored, what minimum rated duration should be used?
questions.explanation: Emergency-lighting duration is selected from the premises and reoccupation conditions, not simply any value in a broad range. Guidance uses at least 3 hours where immediate reoccupation may occur before batteries have fully recharged.

A.text: Half an hour is insufficient for the stated immediate-reoccupation arrangement because the batteries may not yet have recharged after the outage.

B.text: A one-hour system may suit premises evacuated and not promptly reoccupied, but it does not meet this scenario's three-hour minimum duration.

C.text: Two hours provides more endurance but remains one hour short of the minimum used where occupants may return before full battery recharge.

D.text: Emergency-lighting duration is selected from the premises and reoccupation conditions, not simply any value in a broad range. Guidance uses at least 3 hours where immediate reoccupation may occur before batteries have fully recharged.

questions.prompt: Direct acting space heaters:

options.B: Give out heat at a steady rate

questions.explanation: Direct-acting heaters give heat as soon as they are energised. That makes them responsive to room temperature changes rather than storing heat for later release.

A.text: Direct electrical resistance heating can have high running cost, so cost efficiency is not its defining characteristic.

B.text: Thermostatic control cycles the heater with demand rather than guaranteeing a constant heat-output rate.

C.text: Storage heaters charge a thermal mass for later release; direct acting heaters emit heat while energised.

D.text: Direct-acting heaters give heat as soon as they are energised. That makes them responsive to room temperature changes rather than storing heat for later release.

questions.prompt: What does luminous efficacy measure for a lamp or lighting system?

options.D: Luminous flux per watt of input power

questions.explanation: Luminous efficacy is luminous flux in lumens divided by input power in watts. The original keyed option incorrectly said luminous intensity, which is measured in candelas and is direction-specific.

A.text: Power factor compares real and apparent electrical power. It does not state how many lumens the lighting system produces per watt.

B.text: Colour rendering describes how faithfully colours appear under a source, a separate quality metric from light output divided by electrical input.

C.text: Daylight similarity concerns spectral appearance or colour characteristics, whereas efficacy is the numerical lumens-per-watt conversion performance.

D.text: Luminous efficacy is luminous flux in lumens divided by input power in watts. The original keyed option incorrectly said luminous intensity, which is measured in candelas and is direction-specific.

questions.prompt: Protection against solid foreign objects 1.0 mm in diameter and larger has which IP classification?
questions.explanation: The IP4X probe threshold includes 1.0 mm solid objects, not only objects strictly greater than 1 mm. IP4X remains the correct classification.

A.text: IP2X protects against access with a finger and solid objects of 12.5 mm and larger, not the much smaller 1.0 mm probe.

B.text: IP3X uses a 2.5 mm object probe. It therefore does not establish the stated protection against objects down to 1.0 mm.

C.text: The IP4X probe threshold includes 1.0 mm solid objects, not only objects strictly greater than 1 mm. IP4X remains the correct classification.

D.text: IP6X is the more stringent dust-tight classification. Although it exceeds the requirement, it is not the class defined by the 1.0 mm threshold.

questions.prompt: The space factor for cables in trunking should not exceed:
questions.explanation: The trunking space factor limits how full the trunking may be. Keeping it at or below 45% avoids overcrowding, overheating and difficulty drawing in cables.

A.text: Thirty percent is a conservative fill and can be used, but it is not the stated maximum space factor for cable occupancy in trunking.

B.text: A 35% fill remains below the allowable ceiling. The question asks for the upper boundary rather than an acceptable lower design value.

C.text: Forty percent also complies but stops five percentage points short of the recognized maximum trunking space factor of 45%.

D.text: The trunking space factor limits how full the trunking may be. Keeping it at or below 45% avoids overcrowding, overheating and difficulty drawing in cables.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are standard sizes of conduit:
questions.explanation: Standard conduit sizes include 16 mm, 20 mm and 25 mm. Sizes such as 22 mm or 30 mm are not the standard set shown in the correct option.

A.text: This set includes 30 mm, which is not one of the normal metric conduit sizes listed here.

B.text: Standard conduit sizes include 16 mm, 20 mm and 25 mm. Sizes such as 22 mm or 30 mm are not the standard set shown in the correct option.

C.text: 22 mm is a common copper-pipe size rather than the standard electrical-conduit size in this sequence.

D.text: This set again substitutes non-standard 30 mm for the standard 16 mm size.

questions.prompt: During installation, what is the principal purpose of inspection-type conduit fittings such as inspection elbows and tees?

options.A: Provide routine access to energized conductors after completion
options.B: Facilitate drawing in and inspection of conductors

questions.explanation: The original 'facilitate access to the conduit' distractor overlaps the keyed answer. Inspection fittings provide access used when drawing in and inspecting conductors; they are not intended as routine access to energized parts.

A.text: Covers must not be treated as routine live-access points. Safe isolation is required before opening a fitting to inspect or work on conductors.

B.text: The original 'facilitate access to the conduit' distractor overlaps the keyed answer. Inspection fittings provide access used when drawing in and inspecting conductors; they are not intended as routine access to energized parts.

C.text: An inspection elbow or tee changes direction while providing a removable cover; it is not installed as structural reinforcement for the raceway.

D.text: Saddles, clips and structural fixings support conduit. The removable access in an inspection fitting is intended to aid conductor installation and inspection.

questions.prompt: In a dairy washdown area where the wiring system needs high mechanical strength and resistance to moisture, cleaning chemicals and corrosion, which listed conduit material is most suitable?
questions.explanation: The original has a duplicated 'use' and treats one system as universally recommended without environmental criteria. Stainless steel is the clear choice for the stated harsh, hygiene-critical washdown conditions because it combines robustness with corrosion and chemical resistance.

A.text: Enamel damage at threads, impacts or fittings can expose carbon steel to repeated wet and chemical cleaning, allowing corrosion in this harsh area.

B.text: PVC resists moisture and many chemicals, but it does not provide the same high impact, crushing and temperature robustness requested alongside corrosion resistance.

C.text: The original has a duplicated 'use' and treats one system as universally recommended without environmental criteria. Stainless steel is the clear choice for the stated harsh, hygiene-critical washdown conditions because it combines robustness with corrosion and chemical resistance.

D.text: Twin-and-earth is a cable rather than conduit and is not intended as an exposed, high-strength washdown wiring system in a hygiene-critical dairy area.

questions.prompt: At a distributor's service cut-out, how is the earthed neutral normally connected at the intake?
questions.explanation: 'Authorities supply' is obsolete and the original can be confused with the consumer's main switch, which may have different switching requirements. At the distributor's service cut-out, the neutral is normally connected by a solid link rather than fused or switched as listed.

A.text: The distributor's cut-out protective device is placed in the line conductor; the earthed neutral is not normally routed through a separate circuit-breaker pole there.

B.text: Fusing the neutral alone could disconnect it while leaving the line energised and create dangerous voltage displacement, so the cut-out fuse is in the line conductor.

C.text: A single-pole neutral switch could leave the installation live but without its neutral reference. The service neutral is therefore not normally arranged this way.

D.text: 'Authorities supply' is obsolete and the original can be confused with the consumer's main switch, which may have different switching requirements. At the distributor's service cut-out, the neutral is normally connected by a solid link rather than fused or switched as listed.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of protective equipotential bonding is to:

options.B: Increase the impedance of the earth return
options.C: Limit dangerous potential differences between simultaneously accessible conductive parts

questions.explanation: Protective bonding is intended to limit hazardous touch-voltage differences; it does not guarantee that every piece of adjacent metal is at exactly the same potential or prevent faults from occurring.

A.text: Bonding may create parallel conductive paths, but reducing a measured loop impedance is not its defining safety purpose or a design target for the bond.

B.text: Protective conductors are intended to provide effective low-impedance fault paths. Deliberately increasing return impedance would hinder automatic disconnection.

C.text: Protective bonding is intended to limit hazardous touch-voltage differences; it does not guarantee that every piece of adjacent metal is at exactly the same potential or prevent faults from occurring.

D.text: Bonding does not stop insulation from failing or a live conductor touching metal; it limits touch-voltage differences if hazardous voltages arise.

questions.prompt: Where a gas meter is inside the premises and main protective bonding is required, where should the connection normally be made, where practicable and before any branch pipework?

options.A: Within 300 mm of the meter inlet
options.B: Within 300 mm of the meter outlet on the consumer's hard metal pipework
options.C: Within 600 mm of the meter outlet on the consumer's hard metal pipework
options.D: Within 600 mm of the meter inlet on the distributor's side

questions.explanation: Current wording is main protective bonding. For an internal meter the connection is made on the consumer's hard metal pipework, preferably within 600 mm of the outlet union and before branch pipework; an external meter changes the reference point to entry into the building.

A.text: The inlet is on the supply side of an internal meter. Main bonding is normally attached to the consumer's hard metal outlet pipework instead.

B.text: This position would be suitably close and may be practicable, but 300 mm is not the stated maximum distance requested; the guidance allows up to 600 mm.

C.text: Current wording is main protective bonding. For an internal meter the connection is made on the consumer's hard metal pipework, preferably within 600 mm of the outlet union and before branch pipework; an external meter changes the reference point to entry into the building.

D.text: The distance is correct but the side is not: the clamp belongs on accessible consumer hard metal pipework after the meter outlet union.

questions.prompt: When distributor data is unavailable, what typical maximum external earth fault loop impedance Ze is commonly used for design of a public TN-S supply up to 100 A?
questions.explanation: A DNO is not obliged to maintain one universal maximum Ze, and actual distributor information or measurement takes priority. IET guidance retains 0.8 Ω as the typical design value for a public TN-S supply up to 100 A when no alternative is provided.

A.text: The 0.37 Ω figure is the commonly quoted typical design value for a public TN-C-S supply, not the stated TN-S arrangement.

B.text: A DNO is not obliged to maintain one universal maximum Ze, and actual distributor information or measurement takes priority. IET guidance retains 0.8 Ω as the typical design value for a public TN-S supply up to 100 A when no alternative is provided.

C.text: Two hundred ohms is associated with the practical upper region discussed for TT electrode resistance and RCD reliability, not a distributor's TN-S Ze.

D.text: Twenty-one ohms is far above the typical TN-S external loop value and would not support the expected high fault current for conventional overcurrent disconnection.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 allows a number of devices to be used as isolators. One device which can NOT be used for this purpose is:
questions.explanation: An isolator must provide reliable isolation from the supply. A semiconductor device can leak or fail short, so it cannot be used as the isolating device.

A.text: A suitably rated double-pole mechanical switch can disconnect all live conductors of a single-phase circuit for isolation.

B.text: A compliant firefighter's switch is a mechanical switching device specifically intended to isolate relevant high-voltage signage equipment.

C.text: An isolator must provide reliable isolation from the supply. A semiconductor device can leak or fail short, so it cannot be used as the isolating device.

D.text: A TP+N switch-disconnector provides defined mechanical contact separation across the required live conductors.

questions.prompt: Which RCD designation describes a device with no intentional time delay?
questions.explanation: The original grammar is corrupt and 'O Type' is not the current designation. General non-delay describes timing, Type S is selectively time-delayed, and Types A and B describe residual-current waveforms rather than delay.

A.text: Type A defines the residual-current waveforms the RCD can detect, including pulsating d.c.; it does not define a no-delay timing category.

B.text: Type S intentionally delays operation to coordinate with downstream RCDs, making it the direct opposite of a general non-delay device.

C.text: The original grammar is corrupt and 'O Type' is not the current designation. General non-delay describes timing, Type S is selectively time-delayed, and Types A and B describe residual-current waveforms rather than delay.

D.text: Type B extends waveform detection to smooth d.c. and higher-frequency components. That classification is independent of intentional time delay.

questions.prompt: Which of the following circuit breakers would be most suitable for use with circuits feeding large transformers:
questions.explanation: Large transformers can draw high magnetising inrush current when energised. A Type D circuit breaker tolerates higher short-duration inrush before tripping.

A.text: Type A is not a standard BS EN 60898 instantaneous characteristic for this transformer-inrush selection.

B.text: Type B trips magnetically at a low current multiple and is prone to nuisance operation on large transformer energisation inrush.

C.text: Type C tolerates moderate inrush, but Type D's higher instantaneous threshold is intended for very high-inrush loads such as large transformers.

D.text: Large transformers can draw high magnetising inrush current when energised. A Type D circuit breaker tolerates higher short-duration inrush before tripping.

questions.prompt: Which is a common primary distribution voltage used to supply a private transformer at a commercial or industrial site?
questions.explanation: There is no single supply voltage determined by the label 'light industry': many sites receive 400 V low voltage, while larger sites may take a high-voltage supply. Of the options, 11 kV is a common primary-distribution voltage for a private transformer.

A.text: There is no single supply voltage determined by the label 'light industry': many sites receive 400 V low voltage, while larger sites may take a high-voltage supply. Of the options, 11 kV is a common primary-distribution voltage for a private transformer.

B.text: A 132 kV connection belongs to the higher-voltage transmission or sub-transmission network and is not the common primary supply for an ordinary private site transformer.

C.text: Some very large sites use 33 kV, but it is a higher distribution tier and is less typical than 11 kV for the commercial or industrial arrangement described.

D.text: Four hundred kilovolts is a national transmission voltage requiring grid-scale substations, not a normal incoming voltage to a private customer transformer.

questions.prompt: A typical insulator for an overhead line transmission system would be:
questions.explanation: Glass and porcelain have high dielectric strength and good weather resistance. That makes them suitable overhead line insulator materials.

A.text: Glass and porcelain have high dielectric strength and good weather resistance. That makes them suitable overhead line insulator materials.

B.text: Mica is used inside electrical equipment and butyl is an elastomer; neither pair describes standard outdoor suspension insulator strings.

C.text: Rubber and PVC are common cable materials, but ordinary forms are not the traditional rigid weathering insulators used on transmission supports.

D.text: Wood can absorb moisture and generic plastic lacks the specified ageing and mechanical performance required of line insulators.

questions.prompt: Under ESQCR, by how much may a low-voltage supply at the declared frequency vary from its declared voltage?
questions.explanation: The statutory +10%/-6% tolerance applies specifically to a low-voltage supply relative to its declared voltage at the declared frequency. The original omitted that scope.

A.text: The statutory +10%/-6% tolerance applies specifically to a low-voltage supply relative to its declared voltage at the declared frequency. The original omitted that scope.

B.text: The positive allowance is right, but the negative tolerance is too wide: ESQCR permits a fall of 6%, not 10%, for this low-voltage supply.

C.text: This effectively reverses and alters the statutory asymmetry. The permitted variation is ten percent above and six percent below declared voltage.

D.text: The negative limit is correct, but the positive allowance is understated. The supply may rise by up to 10% under the stated rule.

questions.prompt: Which listed energy-conversion device normally generates electricity without moving mechanical parts at the generating module?
questions.explanation: A complete PV system can include cooling fans or trackers, so the system-wide claim is too broad. The photovoltaic module itself is a solid-state generator with no moving mechanical parts.

A.text: Grey-water equipment is primarily a water-conservation system and normally consumes pump and control energy rather than acting as an electricity-generating module.

B.text: A micro-wind generator relies on rotating blades, a shaft and generator components, so mechanical movement is fundamental to its conversion process.

C.text: Micro-hydro generation converts water energy through a rotating turbine and generator; its generating unit therefore contains moving mechanical parts.

D.text: A complete PV system can include cooling fans or trackers, so the system-wide claim is too broad. The photovoltaic module itself is a solid-state generator with no moving mechanical parts.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a number of Solar PV modules connected in series:
questions.explanation: PV modules connected in series form a string. Series connection increases the string voltage while the same current flows through each module.

A.text: Chain is an informal description and not the standard PV term for modules wired in series as one electrical circuit.

B.text: A module is one packaged PV generating unit. Connecting several modules in series creates a larger circuit rather than another single module.

C.text: Set is too general and does not specify the series electrical connection; the defined PV term for that series-connected group is string.

D.text: PV modules connected in series form a string. Series connection increases the string voltage while the same current flows through each module.
